name: Guul Draz Vampire
oracle_text: As long as an opponent has 10 or less life, this creature gets +2/+1 and has intimidate. (It can't be blocked except by artifact creatures and/or creatures that share a color with it.)
blocked_sentences: As long as an opponent has 10 or less life, this creature gets +2/+1 and has intimidate. (It can't be blocked except by artifact creatures and/or creatures that share a color with it.)

Scope: the card's ONE printed line is blocked three separate ways and none of the three is optional. The +2/+1 half alone would be `{"kind": "static", "effect": "buff", "affects": {"self_only": true}, "power": {"const": 2}, "toughness": {"const": 1}}`, which is expressible today -- but only unconditionally, which is a strictly better card than the one printed, and it would still leave `intimidate` unimplemented on a line the residual gate reads as a whole. The card that is already in the hand-written pool covers none of this; it is a vanilla 1/1 Vampire Rogue.

needs.what: the `intimidate` evasion keyword -- "this creature can't be blocked except by artifact creatures and/or creatures that share a color with it" -- as a `Keyword` enum member the loader accepts, plus the block-legality rule behind it in `combat.can_block`: a declared blocker is legal only if it has the Artifact type OR its colors intersect the attacker's colors. It must read *derived* colors and types of both creatures at declare-blockers time, so a creature that has been made black can block this and this creature being made a second color widens who may block it. NOTE (updated): the two sibling needs once filed under this slug have both shipped -- Stromkirk Noble's fixed-quality form is the `block_restriction` static with a `blockers` filter, and Vampire Cutthroat's relative-power form is `Keyword.SKULK`, compared in `can_block`. Neither reaches this card. Intimidate is a third shape again: a relation between the two creatures' COLORS (and one type escape hatch), stated as an exemption rather than a prohibition.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `Keyword` (`engine/enums.py`) is a closed enum and `KNOWN_KEYWORDS` is derived from it, so a card printing `intimidate` in its `keywords` or granting it via `grant_keyword` is a `DslError` at load, not a silent no-op. Nothing in `EVASION_KEYWORDS` is a colour-based evasion. Menace is the nearest keyword and is wrong in both directions -- it permits any two creatures of any colour to block, and forbids a lone artifact creature or a lone black creature from blocking, which intimidate expressly allows. `skulk` is the newest arrival and is the right *shape* -- a comparison between the two creatures, read from derived characteristics in `can_block` -- but it compares power and takes no parameter, so it cannot be reused or parameterised into this. The `block_restriction` static is wrong twice over: its `blockers` filter is a PROHIBITION ("can't be blocked by X") while intimidate is an EXEMPTION ("can't be blocked EXCEPT by X"), which is a negation the positive-conjunctive filter language cannot express; and it is a static filter, so it reads printed characteristics only, while the colour relation must see derived colours on both sides. `protection` (the one parameterised static, with `from_colors`) is also a stop rather than an exemption, it blanks damage, targeting and enchanting as well, and its `from_colors` is a fixed literal list, so it cannot say "shares a color with THIS creature" and would have to be rewritten if the creature's colour changed

needs.what: an "as long as..." condition on a static ability that may read game state other than counters on its own source -- at minimum a `cmp` over a life total -- so a static's buff and keyword grant can switch on and off with the board. Whatever form it takes has to declare its evaluation order in the characteristics pipeline, since the current restriction exists to keep that pipeline acyclic
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `_validate_static_condition` (`cards/loader.py:504-515`) rejects any static `condition` that is not exactly `{"counters": ...}` -- one key, asking how many counters of a kind sit on the source -- and `docs/card-dsl.md` ("As long as...") states the same limit and the reason for it: a condition reading a derived characteristic would let one static depend on another static's output. A life total is not a counter and is not on this permanent, so there is no spelling of this condition that loads. The `if` EFFECT's condition language is far richer, but it is unreachable here: `if` is an op, ops run inside `spell_effects` or an ability's `effects`, and a static ability has neither -- its parameters are flattened onto the ability and the characteristics pipeline never runs the effect interpreter. Nor can a trigger substitute: `permanent_enters`/`upkeep` plus a `pump` would apply the bonus once at a moment in time and keep it until cleanup, while the printed card gains AND LOSES +2/+1 the instant the life total crosses 10 in either direction, including mid-combat

needs.what: the existential over individual opponents already specified in the Vampire Lacerator gap record -- `min_life_of` / `max_life_of` over a multi-player spec, or the general `{"any_player": {"players": "each_opponent", "condition": {...}}}` condition form -- so that "an opponent has 10 or less life" is a question about SOME ONE opponent. Needed here in whatever condition language the `static_condition` item above ends up with, not only in the `if`-effect language
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `life_of` is the only way to read a life total and it SUMS over its player spec (`engine/effects/values.py:102-104` does `sum(ctx.state.players[p].life for p in pids)`), while `"opponent"` and `"each_opponent"` are the same thing -- `select_players` returns `ctx.opponents()` for both. So even granting the `static_condition` item above, `{"cmp": "<=", "left": {"life_of": "opponent"}, "right": {"const": 10}}` would read "my opponents' COMBINED life is 10 or less". In a duel that matches the printed card; in a pod it is a different card, and the wrong way round -- three opponents at 4 life each sum to 12, so this creature would stay a 1/1 against a table that is nearly dead. This engine is multiplayer and this repo is Commander-first, so that is a divergence rather than a rounding error. `min`/`max` exist as value expressions but take a literal list of value expressions, and no player spec enumerates opponents one at a time to feed them
